items.title: U.S. Markets Prepare For AI Compute Derivatives Tied To TSMC, Nvidia GPU Prices
items.summary: Regulators took initial steps to allow investors to trade AI compute futures based on the prices of GPUs sold by the likes of Nvidia, TSMC and Broadcom.

items.title: Trump Opens Door to Hyperliquid as US Pulls Crypto Trade Onshore
items.summary: President Donald Trump said US regulators are working to bring Hyperliquid, a fast-growing crypto platform, into the country, offering one of the clearest signals yet that the White House wants to pull a major piece of the industry’s offshore market infrastructure onshore.

items.title: Trump Touts Clarity Act With Crypto Executives. Why CME Group Stock Is Tanking.
items.summary: Trump met Leaders of tech and crypto firms, including Coinbase and Ripple, on Wednesday. It’s the next move for the executives after an industry-friendly bill stalled.

items.title: Here Are Wednesday’s Top Wall Street Analyst Research Calls: Baidu, Ciena, CME Group, Dollar Tree, Dominion, Fabrinet, Honeywell Aerospace, Klarna, Pershing Square, and More
items.summary: Markets turned south again Wednesday as surging yields and geopolitical fears rattled investors, but Wall Street analysts spotted opportunity and danger in names like Baidu, Klarna, Honeywell Aerospace, and Dollar Tree that traders need to see before the open.

items.title: Kalshi Brings Crypto’s Perpetual Futures Model to Stocks With CFTC Filing
items.summary: Kalshi filed with the CFTC to launch stock index and copper perpetuals, extending crypto's leverage model into equities.

items.title: Trump Pushes For More Crypto Clarity, White House To Host Meeting With Industry Leaders
items.summary: President Trump may attend a White House meeting of crypto, prediction market leaders in lieu of Clarity Act. CFTC event scheduled.

items.title: S&P 500 Logs Third Consecutive Weekly Gain
items.summary: Stocks edged back from records Friday, with investors weighing weaker-than-anticipated economic data against an earnings season that has defied expectations.  Stocks initially opened higher Friday morning as investors interpreted unexpected weakness in consumer spending and sentiment as further evidence that the Federal Reserve won’t raise interest rates at its September meeting.  Coming on the heels of softer inflation data and a cooling labor market, the figures reinforced bets that the central bank will stand pat on rates.
